body: **UPD.** I figured out it's not depending on exists database file (ex. "cacheSchema.db") or not.

I cannt reproduce this issue. Its OK in my local. when `cacheSchema.db` dosent exists, file and table will be created and no infinite loop as you reported.

![screenshot from 2014-09-23 11 57 21](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5828252/4367728/34d347c2-42de-11e4-8ffc-96d260b375d8.png)

Ensure you are using latest version of Yii.
https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/UPGRADE.md#upgrade-from-yii-20-beta please check the first point.

Yes of course, I've installed plugin. I had this problem before changing assets system. At least month ago or earlier I tried to update for the master, but got freeze and thought that's an instability branch error. But now I tried to find problem and posted my research in this issue.

I'll try to reproduce issue with clear basic application today.

I've reproduced that error in the basic application, and found that error occurred if we specify main Yii::$app->cache component in the same DB, for which we try to cache schema:

``` php
 'cache' => [
            'class' => '\app\components\DbCache',
            'db' => 'db',
            'cacheTable' => 'yii_cache',
            'autoCreate' => true
        ],
```

So it's common way.
need to check if a possibly necessary fix needs to change a default value and causes BC. Set for RC or GA.

I don't think we should do anything. This is caused by the custom DB cache which tries to retrieve table schema in `init()`. However, `getTableSchema()` will try to use schema cache itself, which causes the infinitely loop.
In last case I don't use the cacheSchema component.

Can you show part of the infinite call stack?
Still, it's caused by your custom DB cache, not the core code.

In my custom DbCache I just check "autocreate" parameter and try to check exist table or not. So I have question: (in last case) can I use `$this->db->getTableSchema( $this->cacheTable )` in init() after parent::init() ?
Now we are just guessing. I'd like to see the callstack. It really depends on how you are using the cache.
How to do that? I'm not familiar with gdb or xdebug.
Call `debug_print_backtrace(); die();` after hitting your cache component's `init()` method the 2nd time.
Yes, try this first.
